column1: # Game profile of FINAL FANTASY VI (Switch, update 1.2.1 = v458752). Plays on the Mac and on the iPhone
# Unity 2020.3.37f1 (IL2CPP), SDK 14.3.0: the shaders are Unity Shader objects in data.unity3d and the Addressables bundles under StreamingAssets/aa/Switch, read by unityfs.py

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)

# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup (main+0x345cd0) hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as virtual address memory
# and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. The sdk build is Batman: Arkham Knight's, whose node area cut (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) shrinks the AddressRegionManager's node area to 62 MB.
# With the hardware pool (0xCD500000) StandardAllocator reserved 3.2 GB of address space, and on the iPhone Unity's next 16 MB region failed 41 s in (a null write at 0xffffe0, main+0x839d5c).
# A 1.5 GB pool in the 5 GB block: the game maps up to 1.26 GB through the opening, and the alias region is used up to +3.76 GB of 4.375 GB
